title: Make possible to move desktop icons freely, rather than having them bound to a grid
line: Desktop icons can now be placed anywhere by turning off the new "Snap to Grid" option.
explanation: Folder View's desktop only knows grid cells: the Positioner stores which cell each icon is in, and a dropped icon always jumped to the nearest cell. There was no way to keep it where it was let go. A new "Snap to Grid" option (Icons settings page and the desktop's Icons menu, on by default, only with manual sorting) can be turned off: each dropped icon then goes into the free cell nearest to the drop spot and remembers how far from that cell it is drawn, so it stays exactly where it was dropped, also after a restart or a rename.

commits.message:
folder: allow placing desktop icons freely instead of on the grid

Desktop icons always jumped to the nearest grid cell when dropped. A new
"Snap to Grid" option, on by default, can now be turned off so dropped
icons stay exactly where they were let go, drawn offset from their cell.

BUG: 358990

media.caption: Master: notes.txt and report.odt dragged to spots between grid cells; both jump onto the grid
With the fix and Snap to Grid off, the same drags leave both icons exactly where they were dropped
Master: the two drags; each icon snaps to the grid when dropped
With the fix: the two drags; the icons stay where they are dropped
With the fix: the Icons menu has a Snap to Grid toggle (also in the Icons settings page as "Snap to grid")
